gaps.sentence: ___ he had studied hard, he failed the exam.
gaps.explanation: 'Even though' concedes a full clause; due/owing take noun phrases.

gaps.sentence: He works as a waiter ___ studying for his degree.
gaps.explanation: 'While' joins two ongoing actions; 'during' takes a noun.

gaps.sentence: ___ it rains all weekend, the ceremony will still be held outdoors.
gaps.explanation: 'Even if' concedes a possible (not yet real) condition.

gaps.sentence: ___ the price, the location is absolutely perfect.
gaps.explanation: 'Apart from the price' = the only negative in an otherwise positive description.

gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.

gaps.sentence: ___ complaining about the problem, why not suggest a solution?
gaps.explanation: 'Instead of + -ing' contrasts one behaviour with a preferable alternative.

gaps.sentence: No sooner had the applause died ___ the encore began.
gaps.explanation: 'No sooner... than' is invariable; 'when' would be wrong here.

gaps.sentence: He was warned repeatedly; ___, he ignored every safety rule.
gaps.explanation: He ignored the warnings despite receiving them: nevertheless marks that contrast.
